flawed_step: Line 24: it claims that showing the two subgraphs \overline{G} and \partial G are each 3-colourable suffices to show their union G is 3-colourable.
counterexample: Let A and B be graphs on vertices {1,2,3,4}. Let A have every edge of K4 except 12; then A is 3-colourable, for example 1 and 2 receive the same colour and 3,4 receive two other colours. Let B be the triangle with edges 12, 23, and 31, so B is also 3-colourable. But A union B is K4, which requires 4 colours. Thus separate 3-colourings of two parts need not be mutually compatible.
assessment_summary: The proof relies on an invalid union-colouring inference. The explicit K4 decomposition refutes that inference, so the conclusion does not follow.
